audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers carry [Camille, Skill, Gangplank, Gangplank, Camille, Gangplank, Gangplank]; the packet chart and the prose say [Skill, Camille, Camille, Camille, Skill, Gangplank, Gangplank].
audit.why: whys[0] says both of you are weak at 1 (Skill, not Camille). whys[1] says she wins the short trade outright, whys[2] says last-hit safe and hold W, whys[3] says she keeps the trade edge through 4-5 — three Camille rows currently credited to you or to nobody. whys[4] says the duel sits even at 6 (Skill, not Camille). The early section states outright that levels 1-3 belong to Camille.
audit.corrected: Level 1 = Skill, Levels 2 / 3 / 4-5 = Camille, Level 6 = Skill. Both layers moved together with ratings.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.spikes says 'Camille: Hookshot online, level 6, first item' and phases[4].why is generic; the real race in this lane is never stated in the full layer.
audit.why: Her spikes are levels 2-3 (Hookshot stun into the delayed Precision Protocol re-hit plus the Tactical Sweep outer cone) and her second item, where The Hextech Ultimatum (140/115/90s) isolation plus her true damage reclaim the duel. Your spike is Sheen/Trinity Force, where empowered Parrrley detonating a chain out-damages the Tactical Sweep heal — a window you have to cash in before her second item.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why now says Cannon Barrage's 160s zones but does not win the 1v1; the chart change hands level 6 back to Skill and the 2-item race is already stated in spikes[3].

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer names only Hookshot and calls it 'her engage/stun. Cleanse it with Q.' — the ability that matters most, and the wall it needs, are never described. Precision Protocol, Tactical Sweep and Adaptive Defenses do not appear at all.
audit.why: Hookshot (16s at rank 1) pulls her to a wall and knocks up on landing — it cannot be cast in open ground, which makes lane positioning, not cooldown tracking, the real counterplay. Precision Protocol (9s) is an auto-attack reset whose delayed second hit carries the true damage, so her wind-up is the step-back cue. Tactical Sweep's outer half deals extra damage and heals her, which is why Grievous Wounds decides the extended trade. Adaptive Defenses shields her against whichever damage type hit her.
audit.corrected: Wall requirement in dosFull[0].d, dontsFull[1].d and report[5].t; auto-reset tell in dontsFull[0].d; the Tactical Sweep heal and anti-heal in dosFull[2].d; real cooldowns in breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns carried no numbers and pointed at 'your committal tool'.
audit.why: Hookshot 16s, Precision Protocol 9s, Tactical Sweep 15s, Remove Scurvy 22s at rank 1 — those are the countable windows.

notes: All three packet suspectNames are false positives (possessive forms of Precision Protocol, Tactical Sweep and Powder Keg). The content layer twice says you can 'right-click-cancel' Camille's E stun — that is not in Riot's text or the kit flags, so I left it untouched and logged it as unverified. The Camille kit file flags R as 'channel/interruptible' and 'untargetable'; Riot's description is a dash plus an anchoring zone, so I wrote nothing off those flags. Packet win rate here is 50.0% over 800 games; the mirror audit recorded 51.98% over 731 — the two packets disagree.
